name: Simple & Compound Interest
intro: **Before computing anything, write down whether the question wants the interest or the amount.** That single misread costs more marks in this topic than every formula error combined (§2).
For CI, always work in growth factors — 12.5% is ×9/8, not "a formula".

qs.q: Find the simple interest on ₹7,200 at 8.5% p.a. for 3 years (in ₹).
qs.h: §1 — SI = Prn/100. One line, no traps.

qs.q: A sum of ₹6,000 amounts to ₹7,440 in 4 years under SI. The rate per annum is
qs.h: §2 — the ₹7,440 is the amount, not the interest. Subtract first.

qs.q: At what rate percent per annum will ₹1,200 yield ₹216 as simple interest in 2 years and 3 months?
qs.h: Traps table — convert 3 months to a fraction of a year before touching the formula.

qs.q: A sum triples itself in 12 years under simple interest. The rate per annum is
qs.h: §6 — tripling means the interest earned equals 2P, not 3P. Then rt = 200.
qs.s: Tripling ⟹ interest = 2P ⟹ rt = 200 ⟹ r = 200/12 = 16.67%. (Using rt = 300 gives 25% — the trap.)

qs.q: The SI on a sum for 4 years at 6% p.a. exceeds the SI on the same sum for 3 years at 5% p.a. by ₹540. Find the sum (in ₹).
qs.h: §1 — both interests are linear in P, so the difference is P times a single number.

qs.q: ₹800 becomes ₹956 in 3 years under SI. If the rate is increased by 4 percentage points, the same sum over the same period becomes
qs.h: §1 — find the original rate first. Under SI, 4 extra percentage points for 3 years adds exactly 12% of P.
qs.s: SI = 156 over 3 years ⟹ r = 156/(800 × 3) × 100 = 6.5%. New rate 10.5% ⟹ SI = 800 × 0.105 × 3 = 252 ⟹ amount = ₹1,052. Shortcut: 4 extra points for 3 years adds 12% of 800 = ₹96, and 956 + 96 = 1052 ✓

sets.name: Compound interest and the factor form

qs.q: Find the compound interest on ₹12,500 at 8% p.a. for 2 years (in ₹).
qs.h: §1 — multiply by 1.08 twice, then subtract P. The question asks for interest.

qs.q: ₹6,250 at 4% p.a. compounded annually for 2 years amounts to
qs.h: §1 — 1.04² = 1.0816. Note that ₹6,750 is the SI answer, planted as a decoy.

qs.q: Find the compound interest on ₹16,000 at 12.5% p.a. for 2 years (in ₹).
qs.h: Practical exam habits — 12.5% is the growth factor 9/8. Two multiplications by 9/8 beat any decimal.

qs.q: The CI on a sum for 2 years at 10% p.a. is ₹2,100. The SI on the same sum for the same period is
qs.h: §1 — recover P from the CI factor (1.21 − 1), then apply SI. Or use §4 backwards.

qs.q: A sum amounts to ₹9,261 in 3 years at 5% p.a. CI. Find the sum (in ₹).
qs.h: §2 — divide by the factor, don't subtract. 9261 is a cube, which is the hint CAT is giving you.

qs.q: ₹25,000 is invested at 4% in the first year, 5% in the second and 10% in the third, compounded annually. Find the amount at the end of 3 years (in ₹).
qs.h: §8 — just chain the three factors. Do not average the rates.
qs.s: 25000 × 1.04 = 26,000; × 1.05 = 27,300; × 1.10 = ₹30,030. Order is irrelevant — the factors commute.

sets.name: Compounding more than once a year

qs.q: Find the amount on ₹8,000 at 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 1 year (in ₹).
qs.h: §3 — rate per period 5%, number of periods 2. The rate halves and the periods double.

qs.q: ₹16,000 at 20% p.a. compounded quarterly for 9 months amounts to
qs.h: §3 — 9 months is 3 quarters, so 5% for 3 periods.

qs.q: Find the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 4% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 1½ years (in ₹).
qs.h: §3 — 2% for 3 periods. Then §2: subtract the principal.

qs.q: ₹4,000 is invested for 1 year at 10% p.a. The amount under half-yearly compounding exceeds the amount under annual compounding by
qs.h: §3 — you know the sign before computing: more frequent compounding always wins. Compute both amounts and subtract.
qs.s: Half-yearly: 4000 × 1.05² = ₹4,410. Annual: 4000 × 1.1 = ₹4,400. Difference = ₹10. Equivalently by §4, the gap is 4000 × 0.05² = 10.

qs.q: At what rate percent per annum, compounded half-yearly, will ₹6,400 amount to ₹6,724 in 1 year?
qs.h: §3 read backwards — 6724/6400 is a perfect square of the half-yearly factor. Double the half-yearly rate at the end.
qs.s: 6724/6400 = 1.050625 = 1.025² ⟹ half-yearly rate 2.5% ⟹ annual rate = 5%. (Answering 2.5% is the trap: the question asks per annum.)

qs.q: The difference between CI and SI on a sum for 2 years at 8% p.a. is ₹64. Find the sum (in ₹).
qs.h: §4 — CI − SI = P(r/100)² for 2 years. One division.

qs.q: The difference between CI and SI on ₹15,000 for 2 years at 6% p.a. is
qs.h: §4 — the same formula forwards.

qs.q: The difference between CI and SI on a sum for 3 years at 10% p.a. is ₹93. Find the sum (in ₹).
qs.h: §4 — the 3-year formula Pr²(300 + r)/10⁶. Using the 2-year formula here is the planted error.
qs.s: P × 100 × 310/10⁶ = 0.031P = 93 ⟹ P = ₹3,000. (The 2-year formula would give ₹9,300 — wrong.)

qs.q: The SI on a sum for 2 years at 12% p.a. is ₹1,200. The CI on the same sum, same rate, same period is
qs.h: §4 — find P from the SI, then add P(r/100)² to ₹1,200. Sanity check: CI must exceed SI.

qs.q: For a certain sum, the difference between CI and SI over 2 years is ₹40, and the SI for 1 year is ₹500. Find the rate percent per annum.
qs.h: §4, the "also useful" line — CI − SI over 2 years = (SI for 1 year) × r/100. P never appears.
qs.s: 40 = 500 × r/100 ⟹ r = 8%. P is never needed (it happens to be ₹6,250).

qs.q: ₹20,000 is lent for 3 years at 5% p.a. The difference between CI (compounded annually) and SI is
qs.h: §4, 3-year formula. One of the options is what you get from the 2-year formula — that's the trap.

sets.name: Finding rate, time or principal from amounts

qs.q: Under CI a sum amounts to ₹2,420 in 2 years and ₹2,662 in 3 years. Find the rate percent per annum.
qs.h: §5 — consecutive years, so the ratio of the amounts is the growth factor itself.

qs.q: A sum amounts to ₹4,840 in 2 years and ₹5,324 in 3 years under CI. Find the principal (in ₹).
qs.h: §5 — get r from the ratio, then divide the 2-year amount by the factor squared.

qs.q: Under SI a sum amounts to ₹2,240 in 3 years and ₹2,600 in 6 years. The principal is
qs.h: §5, SI case — the yearly interest is constant, so take the difference over the gap in years and work backwards.

qs.q: Under CI, the interest earned in the second year is ₹660 and in the third year is ₹726. Find the rate percent per annum.
qs.h: §4, last line — consecutive years' CI are in the ratio of the growth factor.
qs.s: 726/660 = 1.1 ⟹ r = 10%. A one-division question once you see the structure.

qs.q: In how many years will ₹5,000 amount to ₹6,655 at 10% p.a. compounded annually?
qs.h: §1 — divide, then recognise the power of 1.1. Don't take logs.

qs.q: At what rate percent per annum CI will ₹4,096 amount to ₹4,913 in 3 years?
qs.h: Practical exam habits — both numbers are perfect cubes. That is the whole question.

qs.q: A sum doubles in 8 years under CI. In how many years does it become 16 times?
qs.h: §6 — CI multiplies. Write 16 as a power of 2.

qs.q: A sum doubles in 4 years under SI. In how many years does it become 6 times?
qs.h: §6 — SI adds. Doubling in 4 years means the sum earns P of interest every 4 years.
qs.s: Interest of P is earned every 4 years. Becoming 6 times needs interest 5P ⟹ 20 years.

qs.q: A sum becomes 3 times in 6 years at CI. In how many years does it become 81 times?
At what rate of simple interest will a sum double itself in 16 years?
qs.h: §6 — doubling under SI means rt = 100.

qs.q: A sum becomes 8 times in 12 years under CI. It becomes 2 times in
qs.h: §6 run backwards — 8 = 2³, so 12 years is three doubling periods.
qs.s: 8 = 2³ ⟹ 12 years contains 3 doubling periods ⟹ 4 years each.

qs.q: Under SI a sum becomes 5 times in 20 years. In how many years does it become 9 times at the same rate?
qs.h: §6 — 5 times means interest of 4P. Find how long one P of interest takes, then scale.
qs.s: Interest 4P in 20 years ⟹ P every 5 years. 9 times needs interest 8P ⟹ 40 years.

qs.q: A loan of ₹2,550 is repaid in 2 equal annual instalments at 4% p.a. CI. Find each instalment (in ₹).
qs.h: §7 — discount each instalment back, or use the shortcut X = P(1 + r)²/(2 + r).

qs.q: ₹820 borrowed at 5% p.a. CI is repaid in 2 equal annual instalments. Each instalment is
qs.h: §7 — the two instalments are discounted by 1.05 and 1.05², not by 1.05 both times.
qs.s: 820 = X/1.05 + X/1.1025. Multiply by 1.1025: 904.05 = 2.05X ⟹ X = ₹441. Check: 420 + 400 = 820 ✓ (₹420 is the present value of the first instalment only.)

qs.q: A sum borrowed at 10% p.a. CI is repaid in 3 equal annual instalments of ₹1,331 each. Find the sum borrowed (in ₹).
qs.h: §7 — discount 1331 by 1.1, 1.1² and 1.1³ and add. The numbers are chosen to come out whole.

qs.q: Three equal annual instalments, each paid at the end of a year, clear a debt at 12% p.a. simple interest. If the accumulated value of the three instalments at the end of year 3 is ₹1,092, each instalment is
qs.h: §7, SI version — accumulate forward instead of discounting back. The first instalment earns SI for 2 years, the second for 1, the third for none.

qs.q: A man borrows ₹6,000 at 5% p.a. CI and repays ₹2,300 at the end of the first year. What must he pay at the end of the second year to clear the debt (in ₹)?
qs.h: §7 — grow, subtract the payment, grow again. Order matters: interest accrues before the payment lands.

qs.q: A machine worth ₹6,25,000 depreciates at 20% p.a. Find its value after 3 years (in ₹).
qs.h: §9 — the factor is 0.8, and 0.8³ = 0.512.

qs.q: The population of a town is 1,05,800 now and has been growing at 15% p.a. Its population 2 years ago was
qs.h: §9 — "n years ago" means divide by the factor, not subtract 15% twice.

qs.q: A village population rises 10% in the first year and falls 10% in the second. If the final population is 29,700, find the original population.
qs.h: §9, mixed direction — 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99, not 1.
qs.s: Net factor 0.99 ⟹ P = 29700/0.99 = 30,000. (Assuming the rise and fall cancel gives 29,700 — wrong.)

qs.q: ₹15,000 is split between two schemes offering 10% and 15% simple interest. If the total interest in one year is ₹1,950, the amount at 15% is
qs.h: §10 — find the overall rate first, then apply alligation. Watch which side of the cross belongs to which scheme.

qs.q: ₹8,000 is invested partly at 6% and partly at 10% SI. The total interest in one year is ₹640. Find the amount invested at 10% (in ₹).
qs.h: §10 — the overall rate sits exactly halfway, so no arithmetic is needed after that observation.
qs.s: Overall rate = 640/8000 = 8%, exactly midway between 6% and 10% ⟹ equal split ⟹ ₹4,000 at 10%.

qs.q: A car depreciates 10% in the first year and 20% in the second. If it is worth ₹2,88,000 after two years, its original price was
qs.h: §8 + §9 — chain 0.9 × 0.8, then divide.

qs.q: ₹5,000 is invested at 20% p.a. CI. The interest for the third year alone is
qs.h: Grow to the start of year 3 first.
qs.s: Amount after 2 years = 5000 × 1.44 = ₹7,200. Third-year interest = 7200 × 0.2 = ₹1,440. (₹1,000 is the first-year interest.)

qs.q: The difference between CI and SI on a sum for 2 years at 15% p.a. is ₹450. Find the sum (in ₹).
qs.h: The 2-year gap formula.

qs.q: A sum at CI doubles in 5 years. In how many years will it become 32 times?
qs.h: Write 32 as a power of 2.

qs.q: ₹6,000 amounts to ₹6,615 in 2 years at CI. Find the rate percent per annum.
qs.h: The ratio is a perfect square.

qs.q: The SI on a sum for 3 years at 8% p.a. is ₹1,200. The CI on the same sum at 4% p.a. for 2 years is
qs.h: Recover P from the SI leg, then switch rate and period.

qs.q: At what rate percent per annum, compounded annually, will ₹10,000 amount to ₹13,310 in 3 years?
qs.h: 1.331 should be instantly recognisable.

qs.q: A machine costing ₹1,00,000 depreciates 25% in the first year and 20% in each year after that. Its value after 3 years is
qs.h: Three factors, not three identical ones.

qs.q: ₹3,000 is lent partly at 5% and partly at 8% SI. The total interest after one year is ₹210. Find the amount lent at 8% (in ₹).
qs.h: Overall rate, then alligation.
qs.s: Overall rate = 210/3000 = 7%. Alligation (8 − 7) : (7 − 5) = 1 : 2 attaches to the 5% : 8% parts ⟹ 8% amount = ₹2,000. Check: 50 + 160 = 210 ✓

qs.q: ₹10,000 at 8% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 1 year amounts to
qs.h: 4% for 2 periods.

qs.q: A loan of ₹1,050 is repaid in 2 equal annual instalments at 10% p.a. CI. Find each instalment (in ₹).
qs.h: The two-instalment shortcut.

audit: A2, B1
reporting the amount where the interest was asked, or vice versa (§2)
A3
using a period in months directly as if it were years
tripling/quintupling read as rt = 300 instead of rt = 200; SI multiples are additive
applying SI machinery where CI was asked — each has an SI decoy in the options
averaging different-year rates instead of chaining the factors (§8)
halving the rate but not doubling the number of periods (§3)
C5
reporting the per-period rate where the annual rate was asked
D3, D6
using the 2-year CI − SI formula on a 3-year question (§4)
D5
hunting for P when the shortcut removes it entirely
dividing the wrong way round, or subtracting amounts instead of dividing them (§5)
E3
applying the CI ratio method to an SI question
treating CI multiples as additive — CI compounds, SI accumulates (§6)
discounting every instalment by the same factor instead of by 1, 2, … n years
G4
discounting back where the SI convention accumulates forward
G5
subtracting the repayment before applying the year's interest
H2, H3
subtracting r% n times instead of dividing by (1 + r/100)ⁿ, or assuming +10% then −10% cancels (§9)
reading the alligation cross backwards — the ratio attaches to the opposite scheme
